en: An inclined plane reduces the lifting force needed by increasing the distance the object travels to reach the same height.
Applying oil to a bicycle chain reduces friction between metal parts, allowing the wheels to spin more easily.
Earth's gravity pulls a dropped apple downward because every mass attracts every other mass, and Earth's huge mass exerts a strong pull.
Wrapping copper wire around an iron nail and connecting it to a battery creates an electromagnet that attracts paperclips.
Copper wires conduct electricity easily because their atoms have loosely held electrons that move freely when a battery is connected.
A smooth mirror reflects incoming light rays at the exact same angle, bouncing them to our eyes to form a clear image.
Plucking a guitar string makes it vibrate, pushing surrounding air molecules to create sound waves that travel to our ears.
Heat travels from hot soup to a cold metal spoon through conduction as fast-moving liquid molecules collide with the metal atoms.
Releasing a stretched rubber band transforms its stored potential energy into kinetic energy, causing the band to snap forward quickly.
A seesaw acts as a lever where pushing down on one end forces the opposite end to lift a load upward.
Light bends when passing from air into water because it slows down, making a partially submerged pencil appear broken.
The Sun heats the Earth through radiation by sending electromagnetic waves through empty space that warm our skin when absorbed.
